slips.sentence: Bramble tossed his head and pulled at the reins.
Tamsin, the elder of the two Hales, had always been the one who could read.
Then she took the road back to Corwyck, alone, as she had come.
He still wore the belt that Ilsa had bound round the stump at the ford.
Tamsin swung down from the stallion and walked the last mile into town on foot, leading the horse, with the ledgers on her own back.

decoys: Rook shook his mane at the far bank and stood there, steaming, waiting for the rest of them.
“That’s no mare, that’s a gelding, I’d swear it,” he said.
He had learned to fight with his right hand alone, and he fought well enough that nobody at the crossroads remarked on it twice.
Above the far bank the sky went the grey of a mare’s flank, and then darker, and the first of the rain came down on the road home.
What if Ilsa had green eyes and was born in Corwick?
Ilsa’s eyes looked almost brown in the firelight.
Oren cut the old belt into a strap for his shield once the wrist had healed.
Oren remembered Tamsin binding the stump with her belt, and how her hands had not shaken until afterwards.
“Ilsa bound it, not my sister,” he told the riders, and nobody believed him.
